_: The King's hosts and their orders (hosts.js; Warcraft III's command card, Total War's campaign map: an army is one thing on the map, ordered as one). near: crown companies within this many tiles of each other (and under no separate order) are one host. speed: tiles a host moves each season on an order. men: men to a company of a kind menOf doesn't name, as the ledger counts them. menOf: men to a company by its Freeciv unit type, at full health; a company counts its share of them by its hit points over its type's full (the ruleset's hitpoints), so a host's men are an engine fact (hosts.js menOf; /world units carry each company's men). splitMin: a host needs at least this many companies to split. ships: the hulls that carry a host over water, never part of one (Mac: ships only move armies, no war by sea; realmrules units.ruleset keeps these two, neither can attack). ordersPerHost: orders the King may give each host in one season (supervisor, 2026-11-12: one order per host per season, not one for all hosts; Total War's one move a turn per army). speed 8 (was 3: a far town was 19 seasons away in a 22-season reign; gameplay review #7). A march on a great house's town lays siege when the host reaches its walls (the decree's siege, campaigns.js): the house and the realm hear of it when the order is given (data/decrees.json march.favour, march.others). siegeAssaults: assaults the royal host makes on a besieged town, one a season once at the walls (Freeciv fights each: realmrules script.lua realm_assault), before its captains lift the siege. peaceMargin: seasons to spare when a host stands in the land of a house whose armistice with the crown is about to become Peace: it is ordered home that many seasons before it would have to leave (hosts.js peaceHome; Freeciv sends soldiers in a peace partner's land to their nearest town).
